reviewed_source.note: This is the explicit new review-production-v2 and its separate one-file increment, not a reconstruction or approval of the unavailable v1.

All 12 preimages matched independently retrieved complete cc57 Git source bytes. All 15 packet postimages matched their stated full identities and manifest rows.

The 15-file unified patch was independently applied with exact hunk context/count validation; all resulting complete postimages matched. The separate 667-byte cfg patch exactly produced the final full lib.rs.
Three declared new paths returned NOT_FOUND under the exact cc57 commit; those are repository-path observations, not physical host file observations.
Eleven modified old files are recovered byte-for-byte by removing only named additions. The twelfth, state.rs, differs only in the two explicitly inspected original-client getter fallbacks.
All seven original state current/recovery/phase/reader functions and all four old by-value S/C factories/adapters retain their complete original bytes.

resolved_finding.severity: compile-compatibility blocker in uncorrected production v2
resolved_finding.evidence: The new export was inserted between the old #[cfg(target_os = "linux")] and OriginalCircuitRetainedArtifactCheckpointV1 export. That left the old export unguarded while circuit_feature_current remained Linux-only.
resolved_finding.correction: The separate increment adds the original Linux attribute before the old export, making both exports separately guarded.
resolved_finding.verification: Removing only the new guarded export from the corrected complete lib.rs exactly restores the complete original cc57 lib.rs.

findings.finding: Each consuming seal requires an actual retained completion, exact opaque equality, a present original channel, live peer/lifetime and complete original signature authentication. It sets execution_requested=true in that same channel before Arc::new(self). Original fields, constructors, exchange and readback bodies are byte-identical after removal of the module mount.
findings.implication: No new stream, nonce, counter, lifetime, optional mutex or queue is created. The same aggregate request state is shared. Even the crate-private raw references remain subject to the original Execute-before-I/O rejection; there is no external raw-client/Deref/FD/Execute surface on the bundle.

findings.finding: The original evaluated context authenticates Readback, then supplies its own complete original T and E receipts to the consuming seals. Both clients are removed together from the Version state. Missing either or any partial sealing error clears selection_reader and drops taken clients; there is no restoration, reconnection, rebind or downgrade to a Fresh execution state.
findings.implication: Partial success is fail-closed, not an atomic rollback promise.

findings.finding: Every export, including a repeat export, requires the evaluated purpose, actual Published outcome, original lifetime, the original state lock, original predecessor binding, and original full read. Recovered origin uses read_original_recovery. Export additionally requires an observed publication, an admitted selection reader and Installed/Recovered phase, then rechecks Published and lifetime. Installed or cold Published metadata alone cannot pass.
findings.implication: No new enum/reader shortcut substitutes for the original D/T/E, Artifact/CURRENT and original C owner checks.

findings.finding: Only the two getters gain a fallback to the same sealed bundle clients when the old retained fields are empty. Prepared continues to read its original Prepared custody. The original full current/read/recovery/phase functions are unchanged and still read and compare actual original owner responses.
findings.implication: Sharing does not turn Version reads into cached evidence or skip recovery admission.

findings.finding: New explicit SharedEvaluated variants and factories bind the same complete evaluated context. They retain original live publication checks, owner command-origin profile, initial head/binding, C's complete selector-client checks, runtime handle and four-connection semaphore. Each shared observation again checks context and then invokes the existing actual remote owner methods with the same client references.
findings.implication: Old by-value entries remain byte-identical. The original T/E then S then final Source/Cell order is reused; no attestation or execution authority comes from cached metadata.

findings.finding: The public bundle has two private Arc fields plus the original evaluated context. Its public operations are Clone and actual readonly predecessor reads; only the actual Version host exports it. The context clone preserves original origin and opaque receipt/signature bytes. Internal raw client access is crate-private, and both channels have permanently spent Execute before any bundle can be returned.
findings.implication: This is local same-process sharing. It supplies no cross-process Arc serialization, descriptor duplication, transport proxy, public owner factory, public raw client, signer or new stream.

findings.finding: Original exchange removes its sole channel before spawned I/O and restores it only at its original successful validation point. A competing alias sees the same absent slot and refuses. Cancellation of the actual exchange await preserves that original behavior. T and E retain their distinct nonterminal and terminal error handling; the review does not claim that every error leaves None.
findings.implication: No new queue, retry, concurrency success guarantee, budget increase or silent error-to-success conversion is introduced. Existing run_original_c background reads can still compete with S/C reads.

findings.finding: Dropping the outer await after spawn_blocking has started does not establish that its closure stopped. It can finish readonly currentness reads and the one-way conversion; its result may be lost to that caller while readonly state remains. This is distinct from dropping a nested original exchange await.
findings.implication: Treat cancelled caller delivery as Unknown. Any retained state remains readonly or fail-closed; there is no Fresh restoration or new-work replay. The code does not claim that cancellation joined the blocking task.

tokio_reference.summary: A started blocking task cannot be stopped by aborting its handle; dropping a JoinHandle detaches it and loses the returned value.
tokio_reference.use: Support for the static cancellation interpretation, not evidence of any actual candidate execution.
